label: verify-bm-architecture-gaps

claims.claim: The best passive bio-based skin (Freiburg) has no building-performance number and a short durability record, so the open gap is geometry to solar gain and cycle life.
claims.source_says: it will be important to quantify the improvement of indoor climate regulation in future work. ... The number of cycles tested is still small compared to the entire lifetime of a building
claims.note: Both passages are in PMC11604995; 'best' is the agent's judgement and the gap framing is inference, but the factual parts check out.

claims.claim: Flexible 80A V2 shows +8 percent mass and +3 percent volume after 1 day in water (immersion), contradicting 'under 1 percent'; it is the only catalogue resin with enough swelling for a hygromorph layer; humid-air constants unpublished.
claims.source_says: Deionized Water: 1 day -26 (Shore A) +8% mass +3% volume 94% elongation 89% tensile; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88%. Slabs fully immersed, wiped dry.
claims.note: The datasheet numbers reproduce from word coordinates, but 'only catalogue resin' and 'humid-air unpublished' were not shown (the cube table has no V2 row; the old Flexible 80A reads 0.7).

claims.claim: Mycelium and other living or fungal materials lack a verified reaction-to-fire class and are TRL 3-5 beyond insulation and packaging, so are the wrong first target for a small computational team.
claims.source_says: Full-scale testing in accordance with the BS EN 13501-1 standard is rarely used for MBCs ... Most MBC research currently resides between TRL 3 and TRL 5 ... (insulation/packaging TRL 7-9)
claims.note: Sources support 'rarely tested' and TRL 3-5 for mycelium composites, not a blanket 'no verified class' or any claim on other living materials; 'wrong first target' is a judgement.

claims.claim: Embodied-carbon data are missing for most emerging structural materials, so a transparent carbon sheet for the proof of concept is a real computation-only contribution.
claims.source_says: Only 18% (37 out of 204) of the emerging structural materials reviewed had EC values; less (11%) had embodied energy values.
claims.note: The 18 percent figure is verbatim in PMC13068519 (so 82 percent lack values); the 'real contribution' conclusion is the agent's opinion.

overall: Three of four key claims rest on passages I found verbatim in the sources. The Freiburg and embodied-carbon claims are supported. The Flexible 80A V2 swelling numbers reproduce exactly from the PDF. The mycelium claim is overgeneralised beyond what the sources say. Exclusivity and absence-of-evidence parts were not verified.
